questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Drive to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up in a travel lane or on the shoulder. Other drivers won't expect this and it can cause a crash. Instead, drive to the next exit or crossroad.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?

options.text: A hilly, open road
A residential road
A road in a shaded area

questions.correctAnswerText: A road in a shaded area
questions.explanation: Shaded areas freeze before other parts of the road and thaw out later. On cold, wet days, these spots become icy.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
No parking.
No U-turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn. You cannot turn around to go in the opposite direction at this intersection.

questions.question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and turn your wheels:

options.text: Toward the edge of the road.
Away from the edge of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the edge of the road.
questions.explanation: Turn your front wheels toward the right (edge of the road). If the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the road instead of into traffic.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver doesn't dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: At the center of the roadway.
Toward the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see the road to stay on course. Don't retaliate by keeping your bright lights on.

questions.question: When passing, when should you move back into the right lane?

options.text: When you are one vehicle length ahead of the other vehicle.
When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
When you are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, you have enough space to return to the right lane safely.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should always:

options.text: Stop, listen, and proceed carefully.
Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Look left and right to check for people and other vehicles that might enter your path.

questions.question: When you want to change lanes, you should never:

options.text: Move into another lane while inside an intersection.
Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane while inside an intersection.
questions.explanation: Never change lanes inside an intersection. Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and watch for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
Traffic signal ahead.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake firmly.
Take your foot off the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Release the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other vehicle without needing to brake hard or swerve.

questions.question: When parking on any hill, you should:

options.text: Touch one rear wheel to the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
Keep your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in "park."
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in gear or "park." If there is no curb, turn your wheels so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn wheels toward it going uphill or away from it going downhill.

questions.question: You cannot park within ____ of a fire hydrant.

options.text: 25 feet
15 feet
30 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 feet
questions.explanation: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant. Park only where it is legal and where other drivers can see your vehicle clearly.

questions.question: When merging onto the freeway, you should drive:

options.text: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted speed limit for freeways.

questions.correctAnswerText: At or near the speed of freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at or near the speed of traffic.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rainy conditions, you should:

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when tires lose contact with the road on wet surfaces. The vehicle rides on top of the water. Driving slowly in rainy conditions prevents this.

questions.question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even with a turn signal, don't assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
A small car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, and vehicles towing trailers cannot see you if you drive directly behind them. Increase your following distance. Large vehicles also block your view of the road ahead, so stay back to see around them.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:

options.text: 0.05 percent.
0.08 percent.
0.02 percent.

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08 percent.
questions.explanation: It is illegal for drivers 21 and older to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is dangerous and against the law.

questions.question: If you encounter a dust storm while driving, you should:

options.text: Drive through it carefully, since dust storms usually pass quickly.
Slow down, pull completely off the road, turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, and wait for the storm to pass.
Slow down, pull completely off the road, turn on your lights, and wait for the storm to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, pull completely off the road, turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, and wait for the storm to pass.
questions.explanation: When you hit a dust storm, reduce speed and drive completely off the highway to the right. Turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, keep your seat belt on, and stay in your vehicle until the storm passes.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of other vehicles around you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your driving speed depends on road conditions, weather, and the speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: When entering the interstate, find a gap in traffic, match the speed of traffic, signal, and:

options.text: Expect traffic to let you in since you have the right-of-way.
Merge carefully into the gap.
Wait for the lane to clear before merging.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge carefully into the gap.
questions.explanation: Find a gap, increase your speed to match traffic, and signal. When it is safe, merge into the gap. Watch for other traffic and do not expect other drivers to make room for you.

questions.question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut across all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. Expect to see bicyclists using the left lane when they turn left.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light, if you have not entered the intersection yet, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through before the red light.
Reduce speed and continue carefully through the intersection.
Stop safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely.
questions.explanation: At a steady yellow light, stop your vehicle safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through at a safe speed.

questions.question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if:

options.text: You speed up before turning.
Traffic moves to the right.
Traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You may turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left, if there is no sign stopping you. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves right.

questions.question: You should signal ____ before you start to turn.

options.text: 20 feet
50 feet
100 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 100 feet
questions.explanation: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn or change lanes. This tells other drivers your plan. Keep signaling until you finish the turn or lane change.

questions.question: When driving at night, you should:

options.text: Always use your high beams.
Look directly at oncoming headlights.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it is hard to see at night. Use your headlights correctly—follow the rules for high and low beams. Do not look directly at oncoming headlights, as the glare can blind you.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery:

options.text: After it has been raining hard for several hours.
When they are clean and dry.
Right when it starts to rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Right when it starts to rain.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first half hour of rain. Water mixes with oil and chemicals on the road that have not yet washed away, making the surface very slippery. Drive with extra caution on wet roads.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The vehicle has the right-of-way.
Slow-moving vehicle.
Shoulder work ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow-moving vehicles like farm tractors, road maintenance vehicles, and carts pulled by animals display an orange and red triangle on the back.

questions.question: Turning right on a red light is allowed:

options.text: Only where a sign says you can.
Except where a sign says you cannot.
Only on divided roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Except where a sign says you cannot.
questions.explanation: You can turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it. First, come to a complete stop and wait for other vehicles and pedestrians to clear the intersection.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These make it harder to control your vehicle.

questions.question: On a road with a single broken white centerline, you:

options.text: Must stay in your lane.
May cross the centerline to change lanes.
May change lanes only from the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the centerline to change lanes.
questions.explanation: White lines show lanes going in the same direction. A broken white line means you may pass another vehicle when it is safe to do so.
